name: Jidlaf
title: Son of Nahor
summary: Jidlaf was one of the eight sons of Nahor and Milcah. He is mentioned in the genealogy in Genesis as part of Abraham's extended family. He is a lesser-known biblical figure, but his place in the genealogy links him to the lineage of the patriarchs.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Nahor's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Jidlaf is mentioned as one of eight sons born to Milcah by Nahor, Abraham's brother. This genealogy was reported to Abraham after the binding of Isaac.

keyEvents.title: Family Ties to Abraham
keyEvents.description: As a son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, Jidlaf was part of the wider family circle that connected the patriarchs. This connection was important for marriage alliances in the patriarchal era.

keyEvents.title: Part of Milcah's Descendants
keyEvents.description: Milcah, Jidlaf's mother, bore eight sons to Nahor. These sons formed the foundation for several Aramaic tribes and peoples in the Mesopotamian region.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Rebekah's Family
keyEvents.description: Jidlaf's brother Bethuel became the father of Rebekah, who later became Isaac's wife. Thus, Jidlaf was Rebekah's uncle and connected to the ongoing patriarchal history.
